r.정치 구도: Since independence in 1956 it has been through repeated coups and military rule. A regime that lasted 30 years fell to civilian protests in 2019, and a transitional government shared between the military and civilians took over, but in 2021 the military pushed the civilians out in another coup. The army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces, which carried out that coup together, then fell out over how to fold the RSF into the army, and in April 2023 they went to war. The RSF grew out of militias that fought on the government's side in the Darfur conflict of the 2000s. Today the army holds the capital Khartoum and the north, east and center, while the RSF took El Fasher in October 2025 and now controls almost all of Darfur. The RSF has set up its own government in the areas it holds, raising fears that the country could split in two.

t.why: It sits on the western shore of the Red Sea, close to the shipping lane leading to the Suez Canal, and shares the waters of the Nile with Egypt and Ethiopia. That position draws its neighbors deep into the war. Egypt leans toward the army, while the United Arab Emirates is accused of arming the RSF, which it denies. In September 2025 the United States, Saudi Arabia, Egypt and the UAE proposed a three-month humanitarian truce followed by a transition to civilian rule, but the army rejected it and the fighting goes on. The war has spread to 13 of the country's 18 states, driven about 14 million people from their homes and left nearly 20 million facing acute hunger, making it the world's largest humanitarian crisis. Reports of mass killings of civilians when El Fasher fell have strengthened international calls for accountability.
t.rel: The army and the Rapid Support Forces have been fighting since 2023, and neighbors such as Egypt and the UAE are suspected of backing opposite sides. Millions have fled to Chad, South Sudan and Egypt. With South Sudan, which split off in 2011, oil transport and the Abyei area remain unresolved.
t.korea: Diplomatic relations were established in April 1977. When the war broke out in April 2023, Korea ran Operation Promise, moving 28 Korean nationals 850 kilometers by bus from Khartoum to Port Sudan and then flying them on military aircraft across the Red Sea to Jeddah in Saudi Arabia and home. The United States, the UAE and Saudi Arabia helped with the operation. In 2019 the Korea International Cooperation Agency worked with the UN Development Programme to bring renewable energy to farming communities in Sudan.
t.know: Sudan has more than 200 pyramids, more than Egypt.
etext: It is one of Africa's leading gold producers. Much of the gold comes from small-scale mines that are hard for the state to oversee, and a large share is smuggled abroad. Both the army and the RSF are said to fund the war through gold.

It has long exported sesame, groundnuts and gum arabic. Most of the world's gum arabic, used in soft drinks and sweets, comes from Sudan. Camels, sheep and cattle are sold to Gulf countries such as Saudi Arabia.

When South Sudan split off in 2011, it took most of the oil fields. South Sudan's crude still flows through Sudan's pipeline to Port Sudan, so transit fees are an important source of income. The war has repeatedly shut the pipeline down.

The capital, where factories, banks and markets were concentrated, has been badly damaged, and the economy has shrunk sharply. The currency keeps losing value, sending prices soaring. Fighting during planting seasons has cut food production.
